issues.description: The current Stata entrypoints use a Windows absolute folder, and both current Python processors hardcode a Windows raw-input/output root. The README directs users to change these paths; the selected runtime guidance requires relative paths from the staged work directory.

Stata 18 selects [redacted-path-2e11585158df] version 3.13.5, where metadata-only python which checks report pandas, numpy and openpyxl absent. The current creator invokes both Python processors through Stata, so the full path needs a Python runtime with these dependencies.

The current processors select string-named columns, then use row[0], row[1], etc. on each iterrows Series. With the available Pandas 3.0.6, integer Series keys are labels rather than positions; these selected string labels are known from the source. This is a source compatibility issue independent of the unknown workerId value type.

The raw workbook has headers Duration (in seconds) and Q30_Operating System, while the creator refers to Durationinseconds and Q30_OperatingSystem. Stata firstrow translates Excel headers to valid Stata names, but the static manual does not establish the exact mappings. No failed import or missing-variable defect is asserted.

Both current processors call df.mean() after writing their output DTA. The workerId/output dtypes were not inspected, so this audit cannot establish whether the print-only reduction completes under the target Pandas environment; no failure is inferred from an unknown identifier type.

review_notes: Selected target is the README-documented non-Old workflow plus a separate analysis-only route using the supplied prepared Long and Wide datasets. D0004-D0030 were individually reviewed as Old variants and are optional only for these selected scopes; a broader historical figures/tables target is outside this assessment.

No raw participant rows, identifier values, or per-row data types were inspected. Both Python processors call df.mean(); its runtime behavior is left unresolved because workerId and output dtypes were not inspected. No failure is inferred from an unknown identifier type.

Stata 18 metadata-only query selects [redacted-path-2e11585158df] 3.13.5, where pandas, numpy and openpyxl are not found. The separately available Python 3.12.14 environment has Pandas 3.0.6, NumPy 2.5.3 and openpyxl 3.1.5. No author code or study-data imports were run.

Stata import excel firstrow translates raw headers to valid variable names, but the exact imported names expected by the current creator were not tested; no missing-variable defect is asserted from raw headers alone.

The Pandas DataFrame.to_stata documentation page returned a static-documentation cache miss. This is preserved in probes/public_doc_fetch_failure_pandas_to_stata_002.json as process history only; no incompatibility is inferred from the fetch failure. The packaged Python output DTAs were structurally readable.

The discovery lead at historical artifact jar-61d59a577016_selected_native_source_discovery_20261110.json was checked by exact path and hash and used only as a discovery lead, not as scientific-outcome evidence.

A prior trace runner wrote its result capture outside generation_001. That file remains untouched; its actual path/hash, command, unknown byte size, unobserved subprocess stream contents/timing, and correction withdrawing an earlier unsupported size claim are documented in probes/workflow_trace_runner_path_incident_corrected_001.json. Incident/process records are not evidence references.
Source-reader, malformed-cwd, first historical-review, and rg-path attempts remain in probes as process history only; they are not scientific evidence.
